wins.label: Strong Data Center Growth
wins.evidence: Data Center segment revenue grew 80% year-over-year and 2% sequentially to a record $2.3 billion.

wins.label: EPYC Adoption Acceleration
wins.evidence: Enterprise adoption of EPYC CPUs is accelerating, highlighted by deployments with large enterprises, including American Airlines, DBS, Emirates Bank, Shell and STMicro.

wins.label: MI300X GPU Ramp
wins.evidence: MI300 became the fastest-ramping product in AMD history, passing $1 billion in total sales in less than 2 quarters.

wins.label: AI Software Ecosystem Expansion
wins.evidence: We made excellent progress adding upstream support for AMD hardware in the open AI Triton compiler.

wins.label: Ryzen Client Growth
wins.evidence: Client segment revenue was $1.4 billion, an increase of 85% year-over-year, driven by strong demand for our latest-generation Ryzen mobile and desktop processors.

risks.label: Gaming Segment Decline
risks.evidence: Gaming segment revenue declined 48% year-over-year and 33% sequentially to $922 million.

risks.label: Embedded Segment Weakness
risks.evidence: Embedded segment revenue decreased 46% year-over-year and 20% sequentially to $846 million.

risks.label: Supply Chain Constraints
risks.evidence: We are tight on supply. So there's no question in the near term that if we had more supply, we have demand for that product.

risks.label: Competitive Pressure
risks.evidence: Our nearest competitor has been pretty transparent with their road map, and that extends into '25 and oftentimes '26.

risks.label: Inventory Management
risks.evidence: Customers remain focused on normalizing their inventory levels.
